audit.why: Quinn bullies a gap-close-less Aatrox early and loses every landed-W exchange from 3 on — consistent with 53.58% over 907 games.
audit.corrected: Kept; the interrupt and the cooldowns were added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stage swings were described without the cooldown that produces them.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s. Whether her dash is available is the single variable that decides every stage from 3 onward, and the page never gave the number.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], mid and wants.you[1] now carry the 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault was treated purely as an escape. It is also an interrupt.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away." That means Vault can cancel an Aatrox Q mid-cast and simultaneously reset her to max range — it beats your combo and your chase in one button, which is the real reason a mistimed engage costs you the trade.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.foe[1] now state the interrupt; early names Harrier as the source of her burst auto.

edits.before: Vault away and kite whenever you engage
edits.after: Vault away, interrupting you, then kite

edits.before: Quinn wins Level 1 outright — her ranged autos plus Q (Blinding Assault) blind and harass you for free before you have any way to reach her, and the blind neuters your auto damage. Don't walk up to CS into her poke; use abilities to last-hit and give ground. She's favoured here because a comboless, gap-close-less Aatrox is just a punching bag for a mobile marksman. Minimize the damage you eat and wait for your Level 3.
edits.after: Quinn wins level 1 outright — ranged autos plus Blinding Assault (Q, 11s) blind and harass you for free before you can reach her, and the blind neuters your auto damage. Harrier marks make her first hit on a marked target hurt far more, so don't stand still for it. Use abilities to last-hit and give ground. A gap-close-less Aatrox is a punching bag for a mobile marksman — minimise the damage and wait for level 3.

edits.before: Your kit spikes at 3 and that's your window: when her Vault (E) is on cooldown, E in, land W (Infernal Chains) to lock the slippery target, and hit Q3 sweetspot — that combo kills or heavily chunks her because she can't dash away. But the phase is swingy (Level 4-5 evens out) since a missed W lets her Vault-kite you and reset the poke. At 6, Behind Enemy Lines is only a roam tool, so if she stays you're favoured — ward her flanks, and when she commits you out-brawl her with drain once W lands.
edits.after: Your kit spikes at 3 and that's your window: when Vault (E) is on its 12s cooldown, E in, land W (Infernal Chains) to lock the slippery target, and hit Q3 sweetspot — she can't dash away. But it's swingy (4-5 evens out), because Vault briefly INTERRUPTS you as she leaps off, so a mistimed Q cast is simply cancelled while she lands back at her maximum attack range. At 6, Behind Enemy Lines is only a roam tool, so if she stays you're favoured — ward her flanks, and when she commits you out-brawl her with drain once W lands.

edits.before: Gap-close with E when her Vault (E) is on cooldown
edits.after: Gap-close with E while her 12s Vault is on cooldown

edits.before: Your engage window: E onto her, W (Infernal Chains) to pin the slippery ranged menace, and land Q3 sweetspot before she can Vault (E) away and kite.
edits.after: Your engage window: E onto her, W (Infernal Chains) to pin her, and land Q3 sweetspot before Vault (E, 12s) leaps her off you back to max attack range.

notes: Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
